ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the right triangle $\triangle ABC$ the two perpendicular sides satisfy $BC=6$ and $AC=8$. Three squares are constructed on the three sides of right triangle $\triangle ABC$. If the areas of the four shaded regions are denoted as $S_{1}$, $S_{2}$, $S_{3}$, and $S_{4}$ respectively, what is the value of $S_{4}$? What is the value of $S_{2}+S_{3}-S_{1}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ACFE and quadrilateral ABGD are squares, and the right-angle sides of $\triangle ACB$ are BC and AC,

$\therefore$AE=AC, $\angle EAD+\angle DAC=\angle CAB+\angle DAC=90^\circ$, $\angle E=\angle ACB=90^\circ$, AD=AB, AB=BG, $\angle ABK=\angle BGH=90^\circ$, $\angle KAB+\angle ABC=\angle HBG+\angle ABC=90^\circ$,

$\therefore$$\angle EAD=\angle CAB$, $\angle KAB=\angle HBG$,

Given that in $\triangle EAD$ and $\triangle CAB$,

$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle E=\angle ACB \\
\angle EAD=\angle CAB \\
AE=AC
\end{array}\right.$

$\therefore$$\triangle EAD\cong \triangle CAB$,

Given BC=6, AC=8,

$\therefore$S$_{4}$=S$_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8=\boxed{24}$,

Given that in $\triangle ABK$ and $\triangle BGH$,

$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ABK=\angle BGH \\
AB=BG \\
\angle KAB=\angle HBG
\end{array}\right.$

$\therefore$$\triangle ABK\cong \triangle BGH$,

$\therefore$S$_{\triangle ABC}=S_{1}$,

Let the area of quadrilateral ADHC be $m$, and the area of $\triangle BCK$ be $n$,

Given quadrilateral ACFE, quadrilateral ABGD, and quadrilateral BJIC are all squares, and the right-angle sides of $\triangle ACB$ are BC and AC,

$\therefore$${S}_{3}+{S}_{4}+m=AC^{2}$, ${S}_{2}+n=BC^{2}$, ${S}_{1}+m+n+{S}_{\triangle ABC}=AB^{2}$, $AC^{2}+BC^{2}=AB^{2}$

$\therefore$S$_{2}$+S$_{3}$−S$_{1}$

=$\left({S}_{3}+{S}_{4}+m\right)+\left({S}_{2}+n\right)−\left({S}_{\triangle ABC}+m+n+{S}_{1}\right)$

=$AC^{2}+BC^{2}−AB^{2}$

=$\boxed{0}$
